title: Do people buy games with AI asseta on steam?
author: akirakido
selftext: I'm making a shmup kinda game and I'm almost done. I was thinking of selling it on steam but I'm contemplating whether I should invest in the art and hire a graphic artist. But to be honest I'm not expecting a huge sale so I was wondering whether I should just start my steam page with the AI art. Any thoughts?

comments.author: GigaTerra
comments.body: Right now? Not really, lots of people will attack your game for having AI assets. However that is an reason to spend more time on it and polish it to an great game.

replies.author: -qix
replies.body:
This is mostly a redditors opinion. The VAST majority of people don’t care.

So long as a game is fun, people will play it.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body: I would believe this if you can find an single game, clearly AI made or assisted, that is doing well. I have been tracking some games on the next fest that I know has AI, and it has not been good.

replies.author: akirakido
replies.body: I've heard people don't like ai assets on the next fest, but I don't know if they represent the general public who buys games on steam.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
If that is how you feel, then look at Steam, see if you can find anything that looks AI made that is doing well.

You have to understand that people who pay for games are consumers, and gamers. Gamers are an culture, one heavily influenced by YouTube and next fest. Consumers are on the fence right now on AI, yes more and more are becoming accepting of AI but we are far from AI having no impact on your game popularity.

It is also not just the games them self. In the art world 4 years ago Stylized graphics was the peak. An long lasting art style, cheaper than realism. However since AI is actually better at stylization than realism, even the art industry shifted. Now realism and semi-realism are the selling art styles.

Yes, there is an pro-AI, or even an don't care market, but it is still growing.

replies.author: -qix
replies.body: This is honestly a reddit issue. Maybe also Instagram and X lol, but not reality. If a group of friends see a game in the store and it looks half decent, has fun elements and is reasonably priced, they will buy it.

replies.author: -qix
replies.body:
The Finals, Palworld, High on Life and System Shock (the remake) all used generative AI either in their game assets and art or for coding purposes.

You say “clearly made” but that means either the AI looks poorly done, which of course isn’t going to do well game wise. Or you mean clearly made with AI is part of the games selling point. Which is also irrelevant.

If a game is made with AI assets. But is done in a way that resonates with the player, the average person doesn’t notice or even care if AI is used.

replies.author: Exp5000
replies.body: Don't forget Where Winds Meet MMO which has Chatbot AI for its NPCs

replies.author: -qix
replies.body:
Another great example! Also worth mentioning for people that in that example. The LLM they’re using isn’t hosted by them on large data servers, it’s a very efficient and small stack within the games files. Running on your machine as you play it.

Many people used to have a problem with AI usage in games due to the environmental impact, but that’s not the reality anymore.

Give it 5 years and the ‘niche’ in game development will be studios that don’t use AI assets and integrations. The evolution of technology.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
Palworld made it very clear their game has no AI and distanced them self from AI.

High On Life had refund request for just using AI for small touch ups. They had refunds over this, and they use so little AI there is no need for even an disclosure.

While system shock apparently did show AI artwork, and lost pre-orders because of it. It seams to be an marketing stunt, and no AI content was used in game.

Even Expedition 33 suffered actual losses when people just heard AI could have been involved.

>You say “clearly made” but that means either the AI looks poorly done, which of course isn’t going to do well game wise. Or you mean clearly made with AI is part of the games selling point. Which is also irrelevant.

By clearly made I mean games that are not just speculation, and have to disclose. The Finals is actually the only one you mentioned where we know AI was actually used. Even then they make it clear it is only for development and temporary voice overs.

>If a game is made with AI assets. But is done in a way that resonates with the player, the average person doesn’t notice or even care if AI is used.

Look at those games, many of them just an hint of AI and they lost large amounts of players and money for it. Even the finals downplays it's AI use. You think this is not caring?

The simple fact is AI, and even pre-made assets have an huge impact on a game. We are in an industry where 50% fail flat, as in every 2nd developer is going to fail and quit. It is an coin toss at this stage.

But don't let my words stand in the way, it isn't my $100, and every failure is an clue to success.

replies.author: -qix
replies.body:
You’re shifting the goalposts from 'is the game doing well?' to 'did people complain on social media?'…

Justin Roiland openly confirmed that they used Midjourney for in-game environmental art. It didn't 'fail'… it became the biggest third-party Game Pass launch in Xbox history and a massive financial success, despite a few people complaining online…

Everyone of those games I gave you made millions and have massive player bases.

Your words aren’t standing in the way. People buy games for fun, not for picking sides of a social media argument.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
>You’re shifting the goalposts from 'is the game doing well?' to 'did people complain on social media?'…

I didn't shift my goal post, can you prove Palworld, High On Life, System Shock use AI, Can you prove it? Prove it beyond social media speculation? High On Life while they said they used AI, he stated "finishing touches", and apparently so little it doesn't require an disclosure. 

Like I said The Finals passes, you have an goal. But sure I will include High On Life 2. let's hope OPs AI game is as good as The Finals and High On Life 2.

replies.author: -qix
replies.body:
“if you can find an single game, clearly AI made or assisted, that is doing well.”

“Can you prove beyond a reasonable doubt to a court standard that they used AI, even after the games founder / creator Justin Roiland publicly came out and said so in an interview?”

Also you: “I don’t shift my goal post”

Be serious.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
???

>creator Justin Roiland publicly came out and said so in an interview?

Sure, that is why I included it. You scored I already said so and included High on life, aren't you happy? Is there some problem with what you recommended?

>Be serious.

***I believe, because*** u/-qix  ***on Reddit found AI games that are doing well, I believe that if an game is as good as The Finals or High On Life 2 it can be popular even with AI.***

replies.author: BenTheSodaman
replies.body:
The immediate example that came to mind was The Rangers in the South from a small dev standpoint. 

And then to a lesser extent, Clair Obscur Expedition 33 and Crimson Desert. Though it is publicly unknown how much AI-made or AI-assisted content is still left in their games after a wall poster in each game was called out with COE33 admitting to it being part of their process before replacing it with actual assets.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
> The Rangers in the South

Uh, this could be an glitch with my data, but it shows the game is dead, and apparently died in 2024? I would really like to know if you know something about this game.

replies.author: BenTheSodaman
replies.body: Still listed on Steam for my region (USA): [https://store.steampowered.com/app/3074110/The\_Rangers\_In\_The\_South/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3074110/The_Rangers_In_The_South/)

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
Right, but developers don't take their games down even after the games die, that is why players hate the flood of games, because it keeps growing, never shrinking.

My stats for Rangers In The South is that it basically reached the brake even mark (for indies that is $20K-$40K per year of development), and development stopped after 2 years, with under 20K players, most under 50 hours.

Do you have any other information, like is the developer working on it again?

replies.author: BenTheSodaman
replies.body:
You're two replies deep and you haven't checked the Steam page. Check the page, tell me what two things were wrong with your data and assertions.

Or if you can't access the game, look at this screenshot I took within 60 seconds of posting.

https://preview.redd.it/y5ysa091k98h1.png?width=2440&format=png&auto=webp&s=e415caed94bb1ca4459794ea8b3c0107621e48d7

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
>tell me what two things were wrong with your data and assertions.

I would be happy if you can tell me what those are.

If you think it is the publishing date, my data collector doesn't factor in publishing date, only upload date. So for example 7days to die is an 12 year old game, not 2 years, because it was uploaded 2013 but "released" in 2024. 

However please share with me your findings, and why you think it is an successful game?

replies.author: -qix
replies.body: You are 100% someone who can never admit they were wrong, or even that they slightly overspoke lol

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body: Did you get the extra confirmation? By the way you will notice that here I am only asking about an data point, I want to know why the commenter thinks the game is successful. You will notice I did not ask about the other things the commenter said, because you already provided examples.

comments.author: Big_Presentation2786
comments.body:
Yeah, I've tons of games made with AI and AI assets.
I don't care where the assets come from as long as game play is solid

replies.author: Fun-Marionberry-4867
replies.body: Do you always put the steam ai disclosure?

replies.author: akirakido
replies.body: Usually is kinda obvious no?

replies.author: BenTheSodaman
replies.body:
Not always.

Bigger studios don't disclose it and don't update their pages when 0.01% to 0.1% of their game contains some more apparent AI resources in it. With a questionable amount that isn't as obvious.

replies.author: Environmental_Top948
replies.body: I stopped buying them because I kept running into issues where they work in the beginning then soft lock far enough in that you can't get a refund but somehow the game is overwhelmingly positive with mixed recent. Then delisted after a couple months. I've been burnt to many times to feel comfortable.

replies.author: Big_Presentation2786
replies.body:
What's that got to do with AI assets, that sounds like a bug in the code, if you're unwilling to report bugs, then perhaps early access/ new games are not for you?

They require a commitment of time and effort.

replies.author: Environmental_Top948
replies.body: They're not early access. I also don't buy early access. My points is that I stopped buying stuff that uses ai because it's 90% of the time low effort cash grabs. Like I wouldn't have a problem with it if the stuff actually worked.

replies.author: Big_Presentation2786
replies.body:
>
I stopped buying stuff that uses ai because it's 90% of the time low effort

This is the silliest thing I've ever read..

First of all, you've just pulled 90% out the air.. 
Nearly every recent game on Steam features some use of Ai 

https://aitransparency.scrapeer.com/

https://steamdb.info/sales/?cc=us&min_discount=0&min_rating=0&min_reviews=100&tagid=1368160

Secondly, you're not gonna stop buying stuff with AI in it, because hardware is moving to incorporate AI into graphics, so what you gonna do? Stop buying computer stuff?
Start getting into books and become a pen Smith?

I feel like you're very easily manipulated by misinformation. 

Yeah some games that are made with AI are shit, low effort cash grabs..
But you know what? There's actually statistically more non AI games that are shit, low effort cash grabs..

comments.author: MightyBig-Dev
comments.body: Personally I don’t care if a solo or tiny Indy dev uses ai assets. Went are we acting like these people can afford them.

comments.author: Noble_Nexus
comments.body: Yes they do. The major difference is that they will not come to reddit to say the bought it. Most folk just care if it looks good and have a solid gameplay or features.

comments.author: Born_Particular77
comments.body:
I look at it this way... first impressions matter and graphics is a big part of it. You will lose some potential sales using AI art but if you are just expecting to not sell tonnes anyways then having paid hand made art might not make a difference, and it could cost more than the sales you would earn with better art 

Also depends on the amount of images you need. If you only need a few images, the cost might be not bad. If you need dozens or hundreds of images, cost will be much higher.

comments.author: Euchale
comments.body:
Yes and no. If your game "looks" like AI its going to be very unlikely to be sold, because people will assume that since you are cutting corners on your art, you are also cutting corners on programming, balancing, etc.  
As long as you make sure your stuff looks good, you´ll be fine and it should sell, or at least that you won't have a harder time than a game not using AI.

comments.author: Chaibi_Alaa
comments.body: All that matters is the quality of the game, not the how it is made.

comments.author: Nearby-Document-4987
comments.body: I don’t buy games that use AI.  It’s just stealing assets basically.  I’m probably a rarity though most have just accepted AI is the future

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectful. Removed for AI Art or Artist bashing.

comments.author: lyeeedar
comments.body: If you are even considering asking this question you can't afford an artist. You need to pay a lot for art good enough to look better than ai.

replies.author: akirakido
replies.body: How does asking a question and affording an artist collerate? I have savings but I also have a family, and I can't just use a huge sum from my savings without considering alternatives. If AI art will make enough profit so I can do it full time, it will be the best for me.
